subject: Embedding proxy & governance: PromptWorks partnership handshake
body:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partnership: embedding proxy + governance handshake

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. PromptWorks has a handful of ISV customers asking for a neutral embedding proxy: they want to call a single vendor endpoint that routes to different vector stores and model providers, but they also need explicit governance hooks (policy checks, PII scrubbing, model attribution headers) before embeddings are persisted.

We think Redwood's serving runtime + routing features map well, and we'd like to kick off a short technical pilot to validate:
- an embedding-proxy API (POST /v1/embedding/proxy) that can dispatch to multiple backends
- a policy pre-processor that can run rule sets and redact/transform text
- audit log traces for each request (model variant, latency, upstream provider)

Can you confirm which internal folks we should loop in for telemetry and security sign-off? We're attaching a short design sketch.

Attachments: pw-embed-proxy-design.pdf (1 page sketch)

Cheers,
Alex Moreno
Partner Lead, PromptWorks
---

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Partnership: embedding proxy + governance handshake

Alex — thanks for the note and the sketch. This aligns to a pattern we see frequently. Vanessa (our partner integration PM) should drive the pilot scope; Marissa (partnerships) will own commercial framing.

High-level:
- We can expose a proxy endpoint (we call it a routing adapter) in Redwood Dedicated or Hosted.
- Governance hooks: we support request/response middleware where you can run transforms and tag tokens. We need to agree on: which transformations run client-side vs server-side, and the acceptable latency SLO.
- Telemetry: we can emit a trace per request and a lightweight token attribution header if you want model-level accounting.

Vanessa — can you take point on technical questions (capacity, latency, required auth flows)? Marissa — I'll need a brief on commercial ask (pilot discounts, success criteria).

-Markus
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 13:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Partnership: embedding proxy + governance handshake

Alex, Markus — looping Priyom for telemetry/observability input. Quick technical notes after reviewing the sketch:

1) Proxy model: we prefer a thin proxy that performs routing + policy checks and then forwards to a model/embedding provider for compute. That keeps alignment with our runtime.
2) Policy pre-processor: two-layer approach works best — (A) syntactic PII scrub (regex + allowlist) that runs inline, (B) semantic checks (ML-based) that run asynchronously with a fast failure path.
3) Auditing/Tracing: we can emit an OpenTelemetry trace for each request with attributes: partner_id, routing_path, model_variant, token_count_in/out, latency_ms. Priyom — recommend including a short-lived request_id header (X-RI-Request) for cross-system correlation.
4) Performance: for a pilot target of 100 qps with 512-token inputs, expect 60–120ms p50 if we run only inline scrub and edge caching; semantic checks add 40–200ms depending on model.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration checklist)

Action: Markus/Marissa — decide pilot guardrails (SLA, timeline). Alex — can you share a sample expected traffic profile and any mandatory governance rules?

—Vanessa
Partner Integrations PM
Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partnership: embedding proxy + governance handshake

Thanks Vanessa — quick answers:
- Pilot TN: 1 customer (EdgeRetail) with monthly volume ~250k text items, average 200 tokens per item. Peak bursts to 600 rps for short windows.
- Mandatory rules: remove 1st-party PII (emails, SSNs), flag potential PHI to be quarantined, retention capped at 30 days for pilot.
- Must see per-request model attribution for billing reconciliation.

I've attached a first-pass SOW draft. Please flag any changes — we'd like a scoped pilot in Jan 2027.

Attachments: pw-sow-v1.docx

Best,
Alex

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Partnership: embedding proxy & governance handshake

Alex — appreciate the SOW. A few commercial notes:
- We'll run a 6-week technical pilot. Redwood will provide a sandbox instance (Hosted) with telemetry access. Pilot pricing: waived infra fees up to 500k items; additional usage billed at our ISV partner rate.
- Need a signed NDA and the SOW clarified on data retention (30 days as requested) and liability carve-outs for customer-provided transforms.
- Can you confirm legal contact for DocuSign? We will issue a HubSpot deal record (PW-2026-0843).

If this looks good, I will loop in Legal and create the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — Marissa
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@promptworks.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Partnership: embedding proxy & governance handshake

All — great momentum. Next steps I propose:
1) PromptWorks to share a short traffic matrix + any compliance checklists by EOD 12/13.
2) Redwood (Vanessa + Priyom) to produce a pilot runbook (technical scope, SLOs, telemetry hooks) by 12/20.
3) Marissa to open HubSpot deal + create DocuSign with NDA + SOW edits; legal contact: legal@promptworks.com
4) Kickoff meeting: week of 01/03/2027 (30–45min).

I'll keep the thread as the single source of truth for now. If anyone wants to move to Slack for day-to-day that's fine, but keep the DocuSign and drive links in email for records.

-Markus
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference
